name: Buildings (Overture footprints)
plain: How many buildings the area has, counted from building outlines traced from above.
definition: The number of building footprints whose inner point is in the area.
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico; also 901 barrios

coverage.frequency: One Overture release (2026-10-21.0); the refresh checks for a newer one every 30 days (refresh unit buildings).

method: buildings.py reads the Overture Maps buildings theme, release 2026-10-21.0, for a box around Puerto Rico with the overturemaps package (about 3.5 minutes, no key) and keeps, for each building, one point inside its outline (shapely's point on surface), its footprint area on the Lambert equal-area plane of the barrio figures, its first source and its height. A building belongs to the barrio whose outline holds that point, or the nearest within 100 m (a pier, a building on the shore); 335 of 2,157,363 buildings in the box are farther and left out. Municipios and Puerto Rico pool their barrios. Checks at every build: 1.9 to 2.5 million buildings, 99.5% or more placed, San Juan denser than Puerto Rico, 1% to 30% in a Special Flood Hazard Area, and buildings following 2020 housing units across the barrios (a Spearman rank correlation of 0.6 or more; 0.965 in this build).
source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Buildings theme, release 2026-10-21.0 (https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/buildings/): OpenStreetMap (1,500,399 buildings), Google Open Buildings (536,571) and Microsoft ML Buildings (120,393). © OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation, ODbL 1.0. Barrio outlines and land area: barrios.geojson and the crosswalk (Census).
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 2,157,028. Highest: San Juan (125,872), Bayamón (86,214), Ponce (80,349). Lowest: Culebra (2,743), Maricao (4,904), Florida (7,829).
caveats: A building is one footprint: a row of attached houses may be one footprint or several, depending on who traced it.
Footprints traced by machine learning (about 3 in 10 in Puerto Rico) can include sheds, carports and ruins and miss buildings under trees; see the share traced by machine learning.
The footprints are as of Overture's release 2026-10-21.0, not a census date: a building torn down or built recently may or may not be in it.
Most buildings are homes, so nothing is published per building: only counts, areas and shares by barrio and larger areas.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab (group Housing · Buildings (Overture)): shade municipalities, or barrios (Settings > Area), by

name: Buildings missing from the base map (3D view tiles)
plain: The outlines and heights of the buildings that Google and Microsoft traced from satellite images and OpenStreetMap does not have, so the 3D view shows the whole island's buildings and not only the ones volunteers have mapped.
definition: Vector tiles (PMTiles, layer b, zooms 13 and 14) of the building footprints in Overture's buildings theme whose geometry source is not OpenStreetMap (Google Open Buildings and Microsoft ML Buildings), each with its height and base height in metres when Overture has them, and no other attribute.
geography: Puerto Rico, Vieques, Culebra and Mona (the box -67.97, 17.85 to -65.20, 18.57)

coverage.frequency: One Overture release (2026-10-21.0); rebuilt by hand or every 90 days (refresh unit buildings3d).

method: buildings3d.py reads Overture's own building tiles for Puerto Rico (zooms 13 and 14, about 2,300 tiles, by HTTP range requests), keeps the buildings whose @geometry_source is not OpenStreetMap with only their height and min_height, and writes one PMTiles file. A rebuild from the cache gives the same bytes. Checks: 550,000 to 800,000 buildings at zoom 14, under 20 MB, none from OpenStreetMap.
source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, buildings theme, release 2026-10-21.0, its PMTiles (tiles/2026-10-21.0/buildings.pmtiles on the overturemaps-extras-us-west-2 bucket). © OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation, ODbL 1.0.
how_to_read: Turn on "3D buildings" in the 3D view and zoom in to a street (zoom 13 or closer): the buildings that come from this file stand beside the base map's. In release 2026-10-21.0 the file holds 704,061 buildings at zoom 14 (a building on a tile edge counts in each tile). Town centres are already mapped in OpenStreetMap; the new buildings are mostly houses on the outskirts and in the countryside, such as Cañaboncito in Caguas, where 5,115 of 12,354 buildings (41%) were traced by machine learning. The file is 7.4 MB.
caveats: No building in this file has a height in Overture's release 2026-10-21.0 (Google's and Microsoft's footprints carry none), so all are drawn 6 m tall, as the base map draws its own buildings without a height. The file keeps the fields so a later release's heights are used.
Footprints traced by machine learning can include sheds, carports and ruins and miss buildings under trees.
Where OpenStreetMap volunteers added a building after Overture's release, it can appear twice, once from each source.
Outlines only: no name, address or use is attached to a building, and most are homes.
